title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR 2–3 — omnem mortem / Scripturis; PLAC spiritualis=peccatum / OT
pass_a_gloss: GAR. 2. Since God here threatened every death by which Adam's sin was worthy, why should we not say that corporal and spiritual and eternal were threatened, since the sinner deserves to be subject to all these? PLAC. Every death by which sin is worthy is a death diverse from sin. But spiritual death is sin, and merits death. GAR. 3. Nor indeed is it unused in the Scriptures to designate spiritual death by the name of death, since the contrary is plain, not only from Luke 9:60 but also from frequent testimonies, of which we have already produced some. PLAC. I did not say it is unused in the Scriptures for the name of death to stand for spiritual death: I said only that it is unused in the Scripture of the Old Testament; I said the phrase by death you shall die in that sense is unused to the whole Scripture. That belongs to that reason of mine. He had already praised, for from Ezek. 3:18 and from Hos. 13:1, but in vain; for even if I do not oppose to him interpreters taking neither place of spiritual death, the matter itself cries out. For in those places it is treated of a death which is not common to all men, but of a death into which certain ones incur for their certain actual sins, whereas spiritual death is of all men, and indeed from their very birth, preceding all their actual sins. Therefore those places cannot be taken of spiritual death situated in the privation of original righteousness.
pass_b_english: GAR. 2. Since God here threatened every death Adam's sin deserved, why not say he threatened bodily, spiritual, and eternal death, when the sinner deserves to lie under them all?
PLAC. Every death that sin deserves is a death other than sin. Spiritual death is itself sin, and it merits death.
GAR. 3. Nor is it unusual in Scripture to call spiritual death by the name 'death'; the opposite is clear not only from Luke 9:60 but from many other texts we have already cited.

PLAC. I did not say Scripture never uses 'death' for spiritual death. I said only that that sense is unused in the Old Testament, and that the phrase 'you shall die the death' in that sense is unused in Scripture as a whole. That is what my reason needs. He had already appealed to Ezek. 3:18 and Hos. 13:1—but in vain. Even without opposing interpreters who take neither place of spiritual death, the subject itself objects: those texts treat a death not common to all, but a death some incur for particular actual sins, whereas spiritual death belongs to all from birth and precedes every actual sin. So those places cannot mean spiritual death as the privation of original righteousness.
source_text: GAR. 2. Cum Deus hic omnem mortem comminatus sit, qua dignum erat peccatum Adae, quidni dicamus & corporalem & spiritualem & aeternam fuisse comminatam, cum is omnibus subjacere mereatur peccator? PLAC. Omnis mors, qua dignum est peccatum, est mors diversa a peccato. Mors autem spiritualis est peccatum, & meretur mortem. GAR. 3. Nec vero Scripturis inusitatum est mortis nomine, mortem spiritualem designare, cum contrarium pateat, non modo ex Luc. 9. 60. Sed etiam ex frequentibus testimoniis, quorum etiam nonnulla jam produximus. PLAC. Non dixi inusitatum esse Scripturis nomen mortis pro morte spirituali: Dixi tantum inusitatum esse Scripturae veteris Testamenti, dixi toti Scripturae inusitatam esse phrasim, morte morieris eo sensu. Id ad meam istam rationem attineat. Jam laudaverat, nam ex Ezech. 3. 18. & ex Hos. 13. 1. sed frustra; nam ut ne ei opponam interpretes neutrum locum de morte spirituali accipientes, reclamat ipsa res. Agitur enim in illis locis de morte, quae non est omnium hominum communis, sed de morte in quam incurrunt quidam ob sua quaedam peccata actualia, cum mors spiritualis omnium sit hominum, & quidem ab ipso eorum ortu, antecedens omnia ipsorum actualia peccata. Itaque non possunt loca illa de spirituali morte, in privatione justitiae originalis sita, accipi.
